title.narrative: Multisectoral Action for Returnees and Vulnerable Communities (MARC) in South Syria (Rural Damascus and Dara'). under Envelope 1 and Envelope 2

description.narrative: ltpgtThe MARC project targets approximately 72,405 individuals through ltspangtmultisector intervention in Dar'a and Rural Damascus to address the basic needslt/spangtltspangt and provide life-sustaining services. Assessments highlight critical requirements across sectors such as WASH, Protection, and NFI. Reports indicate the following numbers of PIN in various sub-districts: 32,582 in Busra Esh-Sham, 49,712 in Ghabagheb, 30,960 in Mseifra, 55,403 in Izra', and 189,357 in Babella, all assessed with a severity scale of 4lt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltbgtWASH:lt/bgtlt/pgtltpgtHumanitarian WASH needs are expected to rise due to ongoing displacements, waves of returnees, disruptions in water and sanitation services, power supply issues, and the socio-economic crisis. The upcoming warm season will further exacerbate the water scarcity crisis and increase the risk of water and vector-borne diseases (WVBD)ltbrgtTo address these challenges, the WASH project aims to improve conditions by enhancing access to safe water.ltbrgtThis will alleviate hardships for vulnerable populations and increase community resilience. Also, securing safe and adequate water sources will create better conditions for returnees and those considering returning, encouraging their reintegration and stability in their communities.ltbrgtEPDC WASH project target to rehabilitate, upgrade and provide solar energy system for 7 Boreholes in Dar'a gov.ltbrgt5 boreholes in Izr'a Sub-district (Zabayer, Bweir, Izra' and Mahjeh communities)ltbrgt1 borehole in Ghabagheb Sub-district - Aqraba communityltbrgt2 boreholes in Mseifra Sub-district, Mseifra communityltbrgtAlso, rehabilitate, maintenance 4,500 M.L of Babbela community water network - Babbella Sub-Districtltbrgtalthough to increase the capacity of the targeted locations (Babbela, Izra' Mseifra) water entities by technical operation trainings beside providing them with operation and maintenance tools.ltbrgtltbgtNFI:lt/bgtlt/pgtltpgtEPDC focuses on distributing winterization kits to 1,140 HHs in various communities in Dar'a and Rural Damascus governorates. Throughout the winter season, targeted HHs will receive heaters, Tamaz, blankets, and jackets. Utilizing Tamaz as an alternative to firewood is both cost-efficient and environmentally friendly. Additionally, EPDC will distribute 550 returnee kits to create better conditions for returnees and enhance stability in their communities.lt/pgtltpgtltbgtprotection:lt/bgtlt/pgtltpgtEPDC will continue delivering protection services through its Community Center located in Busra Esh-Sham city, Dara Governorate. The center hosts both a (WGSS) and (CFS). In addition to the static center-based services, a mobile team will operate in the surrounding areas of Busra Esh-Sham to expand the project’s reach. EPDC will professionally target IDPs, host communities, and returnees, The services provided will include survivor-centered case management and psychosocial support, designed to uphold principles of safety, confidentiality, and dignity. Cash assistance will also be provided to survivors to support their recovery and well-being. This project seeks to address the specific needs of (GBV) survivors, including those affected by early marriage, harassment, sexual violence, and intimate partner violence. It aims to improve both the physical and psychological well-being of survivors through comprehensive, holistic support. Community engagement and awareness-raising campaigns will be conducted to challenge and transform harmful social norms and attitudes related to GBV, thereby fostering a more supportive and protective environment. Moreover, the project will deliver critical child protection services, including individual case management, psychosocial support, positive parenting sessions for caregivers, and community awareness sessions on child protection issues. The project will also involve training for community members on child protection minimum standards. To help meet the basic needs of vulnerable children and families, the project complements its services with cash assistance, ensuring that all services are inclusive and responsive to the diverse needs of these groups.ltbrgtlt/pgt
